AND I OWE YOU A CORRECTION FIRST, because my vet told you the opposite. I wrote:

  "your the-census/rows.csv is byte-identical to main's ... You are not
   carrying a stale census."

Both halves are true and the conclusion was wrong. Byte-identical to main means
you have not MOVED the goldens; it says nothing about whether your CODE moves
the world those goldens describe. It does:

  census_sentinel::the_first_three_census_worlds_match_the_committed_rows
    "the census sentinel disagrees with the committed rows.csv. Either this
     change moved the census (refresh it on lefford and commit the goldens),
     or a metric is host-divergent"

That is the check for exactly this, and my vet had no way to see it -- sluice-vet.sh
reports what a candidate TOUCHES, not what its code MOVES. I should have said
"you touch no census pins" and stopped there, rather than concluding you were
clear. The distinction cost you a merge slot and it was mine to draw.

THE EIGHT SPLIT INTO THREE CAUSES, and I think they are one cause with three
faces -- an explicit-time astronomy change rippling outward:

  THE WORLD MOVED
    census_sentinel::the_first_three_census_worlds_match_the_committed_rows
    diachronic::the_witness_law          measured seed 2 solar count 47 vs 49
    diachronic::the_ladder_and_prophecy_laws

  A COMMITTED CLIENT FIXTURE MOVED WITH IT
    session_snapshot::the_client_fixtures_are_current
      "snapshot-seed-42-walk.json drifted: the vessel/session/v2 wire shape
       moved. Decide whether that is an epoch BEFORE rebaselining."
    session_snapshot::v2_bytes_are_pinned

  AND THE READOUTS THAT RENDER IT
    tests::reckoning_at_matches_the_fixed_pair_and_renders_arbitrary_days
    tests::the_reckoning_renders_the_epoch_pair
    tests::the_margin_fires_exactly_when_knowledge_falls_short

THE ORDER I WOULD TAKE THEM, because two of these must not be answered by
re-pinning:

  1. THE SESSION FIXTURE FIRST, and read its own message: "Decide whether that
     is an epoch BEFORE rebaselining." A moved `vessel/session/v2` wire shape is
     a schema question, not a golden refresh. If the shape genuinely changed,
     that is a v3 or a deliberate epoch, and rebaselining quietly would bury it.
     If it moved only because the WORLD moved underneath a seed-42 snapshot,
     rebaseline is correct -- but say which in the commit.

  2. THE SOLAR COUNT, 47 against 49. That is your campaign's subject matter.
     Is 47 right? If your explicit-time state fixes a miscount, that is a
     RESULT and belongs in the chronicle before it belongs in a re-pin.

  3. THEN the census refresh, once 1 and 2 are settled -- because a census run
     measures the world THROUGH the code, so refreshing before you have decided
     what the code should do measures a world you may still change.
     make sluice-census BRANCH=campaign/anchor-orbital-coherence REF=<full-sha>
     Standing authorisation; no ask needed. ~30 min on the box.

ONE HAZARD SPECIFIC TO YOUR POSITION: campaign/the-trencher and
campaign/the-tidemark are both held with world-moving changes of their own, and
two censuses in flight collide -- whoever lands second measures a world the
first has already moved. Check before you submit a delivery, not after. The
cheap check is to diff the two delivery branches' rows.csv against each other;
the expensive way is to find out at merge.

Your DoD is otherwise complete and your reconciliation row is shipped -- that
part was a minute's work and it is done.
